correctness.rationale: Fix the exact path; deletion of its edges bijects trees containing it with uniformly sampled rooted forests. The matrix-tree minor nI-J proves F(n,r)=r n^(n-r-1), including r=n by direct convention. Deleting an off-path leaf counts (n-1)F(n-1,r); isolating a marked endpoint counts F(n-1,r-1); internal path vertices cannot be leaves. Dividing by F(n,r), summing and averaging over paths proves the exact mean with all quantifiers. Algebraic subtraction gives the sign factor 2(n-1)-r^2(r-1); strict monotonicity of this cubic on integer r≥2 proves unimodality, one/two modes, tied-integer characterization, and cube-root asymptotics. Independently enumerating all n^ (n-2) Prüfer trees through n=8 and exact increments through n=350 passed 60,859 rational assertions. Finite tests do not establish the infinite claim; the proof does.

originality.rationale: Comparison of the complete new statement against the nearest full published endpoint-degree conditional law, the primary 2020 distance-profile paper, the primary leaf-CLT paper and the classical forest counts reveals no direct theorem covering the global leaf-count regression and its cube-root mode. The known endpoint law contributes one term only. The classic counting identity is credited as a proof ingredient rather than a new discovery. Multiple topic, synonym, formula, and exact-result searches found no stronger result. Historical priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: An older joint leaf-distance generating function or obscure finite-tree statistic could implicitly yield the entire expression and cubic threshold; no claim of exhaustive historical uniqueness.

Part of the proof is an elementary application of classic Cayley–Rényi rooted-forest enumeration; the claimed contribution is the global conditional regression and sharp cubic-root sign/mode classification, not the forest count or endpoint conditional law.

value.rationale: The number of leaves is a canonical tree-sparsity statistic and marked-pair separation is a canonical distance observable. Earlier endpoint-degree regression is monotone, but the global leaf count has a counterintuitive nonmonotone conditional profile, already increasing from distance one to two for every n≥4. An exact complete classification of its regression turning point, ties, and (2n)^(1/3) maximizer provides a natural finite-size dependence boundary in an atypically short-distance regime, not an arbitrary slice of parameters. This profile is not supplied by marginal leaf CLTs or distance-profile limits; it clarifies the contrast between local endpoint and global structure.
